extracted.intended_audience: NSF-funded researchers (grantees) and university/organizational communications staff preparing public-facing press releases and science writing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for NSF grantees on preparing public-facing science writing and press releases that meet NSF public engagement expectations, including required acknowledgments, accuracy, plain-language standards, multimedia, story angles, and distribution steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF Acknowledgment
rubrics_metrics.description: "This research was supported by the National Science Foundation under grant XXXXX"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required in all NSF-funded research releases; should appear in body of release. Use the specified language and include the grant number. Logo usage is subject to separate guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo usage subject to guidelines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using NSF logo, follow NSF's logo and branding rules (seek specific guidance from NSF communications or institutional PR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Accuracy (header)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure statements in the release accurately reflect the science and findings; see specific items below (conclusions, methods, limitations, effect sizes, funding, co-author credit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions match underlying paper
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not overstate or generalize results beyond what the study supports; ensure press release conclusions are consistent with the evidence presented in the primary publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology summarized
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise, accurate summary of methods used sufficient for public understanding without misrepresenting rigor or limitations; include key approach elements that bear on interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations stated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly mention important limitations, uncertainties, or caveats so readers understand the bounds of the findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect sizes given properly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report magnitude of effects or practical significance accurately rather than relying solely on statistical significance; avoid misleading phrasing that exaggerates impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding disclosed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge funding sources (beyond the NSF acknowledgment when applicable) to be transparent about support and potential influences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-author institutions credited
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and credit collaborating institutions and partners appropriately in the release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain Language Standards (header)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use public-friendly writing practices; see specific plain-language items below for measurable standards and stylistic guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 8th-grade reading level
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target an approximate 8th-grade reading level to maximize public accessibility; use short sentences and common vocabulary when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer active constructions to improve clarity and engagement; avoid overly passive or bureaucratic phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete examples for abstract concepts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrate abstract ideas with tangible examples to help non-expert readers grasp the significance and mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define technical terms
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When technical terms are necessary, provide simple definitions or analogies to make them understandable to a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use analogies appropriately
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogies can clarify but should not mislead; choose analogies that accurately reflect the core idea without introducing major inaccuracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual aids for complex concepts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use figures, diagrams, or other visuals to explain mechanisms or relationships that are difficult to convey in text alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Angles That Work (header)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested thematic angles that make research more compelling and newsworthy for public and media audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-world applications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight practical uses, impacts, or applied benefits of the research to show relevance to everyday life or societal challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connection to current events
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie research findings to timely news, trends, or policy discussions where appropriate to increase interest and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational opportunities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize ways the research can be used for learning, curricula, teacher resources, or student engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizen science components
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, describe how the public can participate or contribute to the research (recruitment, data collection, observation).

rubrics_metrics.name: International collaboration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note cross-border partnerships to underscore scale, diversity of perspectives, or global relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diverse research teams
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight team diversity when relevant (disciplinary, institutional, demographic) as part of broader impact or inclusivity narratives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia Recommendations (header)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on visual and audiovisual assets that improve engagement and comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher photos (with consent)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include portraits of researchers where appropriate, ensuring written consent and compliance with privacy/permissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lab/field site images
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide contextual images that show research environments, equipment, or fieldwork to give readers a sense of place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualizations of findings
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use charts, graphs, maps or other data visualizations that accurately represent results and are labeled for a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animations for mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short animations to depict dynamic processes or mechanisms that are hard to capture in static images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video of researchers explaining
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short videos of researchers describing the work can humanize the story and provide quotable soundbites for media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infographics for data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design simple infographics to summarize key metrics or findings for sharing on web and social platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution Recommendations (header)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested channels and coordination steps to maximize reach and ensure appropriate review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with university PR office
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with your institutional communications or media relations office to align messaging, approvals, and outreach plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF Office of Legislative and Public Affairs (OLPA) review
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF Office of Legislative and Public Affairs (OLPA) review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with NSF OLPA for review as required; follow NSF processes for pre-release review when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: EurekAlert posting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider posting to EurekAlert! to reach science media; follow EurekAlert! submission rules and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire syndication for SEO
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use wire services to increase search discoverability and syndication, while respecting embargo and review policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media amplification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan social posts and shareable visuals to extend reach; tailor messaging to platform audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local press for regional angles
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target local/regional media when research has local relevance or institutional ties to boost pick-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric (NSF) — NSF acknowledgment included
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of NSF's summary quality checklist; ensure the required NSF language appears in the release body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric (NSF) — Scientific accuracy verified
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm that statements are consistent with the science, methods, and conclusions; cross-check with authors and source publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric (NSF) — Plain language for public
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release should be written for a public audience (target ~8th-grade level), avoiding jargon and employing clear explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric (NSF) — Multimedia rich
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appropriate multimedia assets (photos, visuals, video) to enhance comprehension and distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric (NSF) — Real-world relevance shown
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how the research connects to real-world problems, applications, or benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric (NSF) — Methodology summarized
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefly describe how the research was conducted to give context to the findings without overloading the public-facing copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric (NSF) — Limitations stated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include essential caveats and boundaries of the research to avoid misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Rubric (NSF) — Educational hooks included
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate elements that facilitate educational use (classroom links, activities, or resources) where relevant.
